The web source's `typeof document !== 'undefined' && document.documentElement` guard becomes `const doc = webDocument(); if (doc && doc.documentElement)` — semantically identical. The `setAttribute('dir', dir)` write, the `if (lang) setAttribute('lang', String(lang))` nested write, and the final `return dir` are ported byte-for-byte. webDocument() reads `(globalThis as {document?: WebLikeDocument}).document` (minimal WebLikeDocument/WebLikeElement surfaces declared so it typechecks without the DOM lib, which is absent from @react-native/typescript-config). Under Hermes/native `globalThis.document` is undefined -> no side effects, returns dir (the documented non-browser path). Under the react-native-web build the real document is present so `<html dir>`/`<html lang>` are written exactly as on web. I18nManager.forceRTL was deliberately NOT added: it is a heavy global side effect that would violate the source's 'no side effects in non-browser contexts' contract and belongs to a native i18n bootstrap, not this 1:1 helper port.

The lone `document` dependency degrades to a documented no-op under Hermes via the globalThis accessor while retaining full web parity under react-native-web. No DOM-only module, browser HTML element, Recharts, Leaflet, react-leaflet, or old web-UI component is imported.
